name: Scout Ames
life: “I still remember asking a retired pilot to lend a boat his good name.” Thursday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Scout keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I own the boat. I want her to keep a title because the buyers know her, and she wants a real desk with work on it.
appearance: Scout has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for silver temples and a dark fringe. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. In conversation Scout presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Scout keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Scout wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To agree a real office assignment.
family: Willa Rizzo is Scout’s cousin raised in the same household. Scout asks before bringing somebody along. Willa can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Willa says, “I was the neighbor who opened a door for her.”
connections: Emery Fields. The boat's owner gets a real office assignment costed by the marine accountant.

reactions.situation: An owner offers the former skipper a title with no clear duties
reactions.response: Scout asks what actual work, hours and wage go with the shore title.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Scout asks one close relative to check in privately instead of stopping the party for a public inquiry.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Scout offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
